traits.notes: The seedling exhibits distinct whorled phyllotaxy with lanceolate, rugose leaves that have prominent pinnate venation. The leaves appear to be clustered at the nodes. The stem is green and herbaceous.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves, appearing as a cluster of 5 to 7, clearly radiate from a single node in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are arranged in tight whorls along the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade attached to the stem, not divided into leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins appear smooth without teeth)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate to oblanceolate (leaves are widest beyond the middle and taper towards the base)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute to acuminate (tipping to a distinct point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (wedge-shaped, tapering gradually to the petiole)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a single midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent and clearly visible (venation is impressed on the upper surface, creating a rugose appearance; numerous secondary veins extend from the midrib)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): rugose (surface appears wrinkled due to the prominent venation)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are very short, appearing almost sessile)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears thin, green, and soft)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the stem)
    19.	Stem color: green
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no clear stipules visible at the nodes)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits distinct whorled phyllotaxy with lanceolate, rugose leaves that have prominent pinnate venation. The leaves appear to be clustered at the nodes. The stem is green and herbaceous.
